<h2 id="h_01JN4GXFMZXN144BGJZNCZRW2C"><strong><span class="wysiwyg-underline"><span style="color: windowtext;">Content moderation (Art. 15(1)(c) DSA) & Automated content moderation (Art. 15(1)(e) DSA)</span></span></strong></h2>
<p id="h_01JQ4NZ37HQEXDEHK97R17R5CC"><span style="color: windowtext;">We use a combination of automated tools, artificial intelligence, and human review to help protect our community from illegal content. While all content available on the platform is reviewed by human moderators prior to publishing, we also have additional layers of moderation which audit material on our live platform for any potential violations of our Terms of Service.</span></p>
<p>The accuracy of content moderation is largely unaffected by Member State language due to our extensive use of automated tools and human moderation. Internal statistics show no significant differences between languages. Offenses are largely language independent.</p>
<p id="h_01JQ4K1EBKRJN6PM96CG70TDGB">Automated tools are used to help inform our Trust & Safety and human moderation teams in making a manual decision. For example, when an applicable automated tool detects a match between an uploaded piece of content to one in a hash list of previously identified illegal material, an internal human verification process takes place prior to the decisioning of the particular piece of content.</p>
<p><strong>Indicators of accuracy, errors and safeguards</strong></p>
<p>The majority of automated tools provide information to human moderators to aid them when making a final decision on whether or not to approve a piece of content for publication. Along with our extensive moderator training program, we also seek and highlight any patterns in moderation outcomes within particular categories, or from an individual moderator. Moderation decisions that were subsequently overturned are logged and used as part of a feedback cycle with the moderation team.</p>
<p>Content from overturned decisions is re-reviewed to look for possible patterns with the application of particular standards or guidelines, or with particular members of the moderation team. Errors relating to an individual moderator may be followed by retraining and/or disciplinary procedures as applicable and depending upon the severity of the error and according to documented internal procedures.</p>
<p>This constant check and review cycle ensures that any errors are handled appropriately, and training and documentation are kept up to date.</p>
<p><strong>Automated Tools</strong></p>
<p style="background-color: white;">Pornhub's content moderation process includes an extensive team of human moderators dedicated to reviewing every single upload before it is published, a thorough system for flagging, reviewing, and removing illegal material, parental controls, and the utilization of a variety of automated detection technologies for known and previously identified, or potentially inappropriate content. Specifically:</p>
<p class="wysiwyg-text-align-justify"><strong><span style="color: black;">Hash-list tools – known illegal material</span></strong></p>
<p class="wysiwyg-text-align-justify"><span style="color: black;">We use a variety of tools that scan incoming images and videos against hash-lists provided by NGOs. If there is a match, then content is blocked before publication.</span></p>
<ul>
<li style="list-style-type: none;">
<ul style="list-style-type: disc;">
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">CSAI Match</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: YouTube’s proprietary <a href="https://www.youtube.com/csai-match/">technology</a> for combating Child Sexual Abuse Imagery online.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">PhotoDNA</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: <a href="https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/photodna">Microsoft’s technology</a> that aids in finding and removing known images of child exploitation.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">Safer</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: In November 2020, we became the first adult content platform to partner with <a href="https://www.thorn.org/">Thorn</a>, allowing us to begin using its <a href="https://safer.io/">Safer</a> product on our platforms, adding an additional layer of protection in our robust compliance and content moderation process. Safer joins the list of technologies that our platforms utilize to help protect visitors from unwanted or illegal material.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">Instant Image Identifier</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: The Centre for Expertise on Online Sexual Child Abuse (<a href="https://offlimits.nl/">Offlimits</a>) tool, commissioned by the European Commission, detects known child abuse imagery using a triple verified database.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<span style="color: black;"><a href="https://www.missingkids.org/"><strong>NCMEC</strong></a></span><strong><span style="color: black;"> Hash Sharing</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: NCMEC’s database of known CSAM hashes, including hashes submitted by individuals who fingerprinted their own underage content via NCMEC’s <a href="https://takeitdown.ncmec.org/">Take It Down</a> service.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<span style="color: black;"><a href="https://www.stopncii.org/"><strong>StopNCII.org</strong></a></span><span style="color: black;">: A global initiative (developed by Meta & SWGfL) that prevents the spread of non-consensual intimate images (NCII) online. If any adult (18+) is concerned about their intimate images (or videos) being shared online without consent, they can create a digital fingerprint of their own material and prevent it from being shared across participating platforms.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<span style="color: black;"><a href="https://www.iwf.org.uk/"><strong>Internet Watch Foundation</strong></a></span><strong><span style="color: black;"> (IWF) Hash List</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: IWF’s database of known CSAM, sourced from hotline reports and the UK Home Office’s Child Abuse Image Database.</span>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p class="wysiwyg-text-align-justify"><strong><span style="color: black;">AI tools – unknown illegal material</span></strong></p>
<p class="wysiwyg-text-align-justify"><span style="color: black;">We utilise several tools that use AI to estimate the ages of performers. The output from these tools assists content moderators in their decision allow publication of uploaded content. Specifically: </span></p>
<p class="wysiwyg-text-align-justify"> </p>
<ul>
<li style="list-style-type: none;">
<ul style="list-style-type: disc;">
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">Google Content Safety API</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: Google's </span><span style="color: black;"><a href="https://protectingchildren.google/intl/en/">artificial intelligence tool</a></span><span style="color: black;"> that helps detect illegal imagery.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">Age Estimation</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: We also utilize age estimation capabilities to analyze content uploaded to our platform using a combination of internal proprietary software and external technology, provided by AWS and PrivateID to strengthen the varying methods we use to prevent the upload and publication of potential or actual CSAM.</span>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p class="wysiwyg-text-align-justify"><strong><span style="color: black;">Fingerprinting tools</span></strong></p>
<p class="wysiwyg-text-align-justify">In addition to hashes received from NGOs, we also use fingerprint databases to prevent previously prohibited material from being re-uploaded. Images and videos removed during the moderation process, or subsequently removed post publication are fingerprinted using the following tools to prevent re-publication. Content may also be proactively fingerprinted with these tools.</p>
<ul>
<li style="list-style-type: none;">
<ul style="list-style-type: disc;">
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">Safeguard</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: Safeguard is Aylo’s proprietary image recognition technology designed with the purpose of combatting both child sexual abuse imagery and non-consensual content, by preventing the re-uploading of previously fingerprinted content to our platform.</span>
</li>
<li style="background-color: white;">
<strong><span style="color: black;">MediaWise</span></strong><span style="color: black;">: <a href="https://www.vobilegroup.com/">Vobile</a>’s fingerprinting software that scans any new uploads for potential matches to unauthorized materials to protect previously fingerprinted  videos from being uploaded/re-uploaded to the platform.</span>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>

<h2 id="h_01JN4HJP6Z92CK8EQ3187EDDCX"><strong><span class="wysiwyg-underline">Human resources (Art. 42(2)(a) and (b) DSA</span></strong></h2>
<p>It is vital to note that images and videos are not published on the platform until they have been reviewed by a human moderator, and that our moderators are not subjected to any content review quotas. They are directed to review content and approve it if they’ve determined that the content does not violate our terms of service. Therefore, increasing the number of moderators would primarily impact the speed at which content is published on Pornhub, with little additional effect on the volume of illegal or incompatible content that is actually disseminated.</p>
<p><strong>Qualifications and linguistic expertise of HR dedicated to content moderation </strong></p>
<p><span style="color: #242424; background-color: white;">All moderators review and assess content in a wide variety of languages and employ several tools to assess this content. All metadata is scanned against our Banned Word Service which contains a library of over 40,000 banned terms across more than 40 languages (Including 21 EU languages) prior to reaching moderators. Moderators then employ translation tools to evaluate the metadata to ensure that the text is compliant. Audio content is assessed by moderators who either use translation/transcription tools or who understand the spoken language in the content. In cases where the audio content cannot be understood the content is rejected as we are unable to meaningfully evaluate potential compliance issues. In all cases moderation is a collaborative task where moderators are encouraged to solicit opinions from their co-workers, senior team members, leads, and managers when reviewing content.</span></p>

<p><strong>Training and support given to content moderation HR</strong></p>
<p style="background-color: white;"><span style="color: #242424;">All moderators receive extensive training over a 3-month period that involves theoretical and practical exercises, job shadowing, and a final exam that requires a perfect score to pass. Once the fundamentals of the compliance guidelines are confirmed the moderators are then supervised on all their review for a period of time. Any moderation errors are addressed and corrected to ensure consistent application of the guidelines.</span></p>
<p style="background-color: white;"><span style="color: #242424;">We use two different virtual care platforms (North America & Europe) that give moderators access to a variety of health and wellness professionals. We also use an additional program which provides moderators with further, complementary support and tailored wellness programs consisting of fitness/nutrition/life coaches, counsellors, and medical professionals. </span></p>

        <article class="article clearfix" itemscope="" itemtype="http://schema.org/Article">
          <header class="article-header">
            <h1 class="article__title" itemprop="name">
              
              2024 Transparency Report (Second Half)
            </h1>
            

            <div class="article-meta">
              <div class="article-meta__col article-meta__col--main">
                <div class="entry-info">
                  
                  
                </div>
              </div>
            </div>
          </header>

          <div class="article__body markdown" itemprop="articleBody" data-article="">
            <p class="MsoNoSpacing" style="text-align: right;"><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small">July 1, 2024 – December 31, 2024</span></p>
<p>For Pornhub, nothing is more important than the safety of our community. Upholding our core values of <strong>consent</strong><strong>, </strong><strong>freedom of sexual expression</strong><strong>, </strong><strong>authenticity</strong><strong>, </strong><strong>originality</strong><strong>, </strong>and <strong>diversity</strong> is only possible through the continual efforts to ensure the safety of our users and our platform. Consequently, we have always been committed to preventing and eliminating illegal content, including non-consensual material and child sexual abuse material (CSAM). Every online platform has the moral responsibility to join this fight, and it requires collective action and constant vigilance.</p>
<p>Over the years, we have put in place robust measures to protect our platform from abuse. We are constantly improving our Trust and Safety policies to better identify, flag, remove, review, and report illegal or abusive material. We are committed to doing all that we can to ensure a safe online experience for our users, which involves a concerted effort to innovate and always striving to do more.</p>
<p>As part of our efforts and dedication to Trust and Safety, we feel it is important to provide information about our Trust and Safety initiatives, technologies, moderation practices and how our platform responds to harmful content. This Transparency Report provides these insights and builds upon our previous reports. Further information can be found in other sections of our Trust and Safety Center, including <a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/6017547823763-Pornhub-Literacy">resources</a> about our community, keeping our platform safe, and our <a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/4419900587155-About-our-Policies-and-Related-Guidelines">policies</a>.</p>
<p>We are committed to being as transparent as possible and to being a leader in eradicating abusive content from the internet. We will continue to do our part to create a safe space for our users.</p>
<div class="accordion accordion--default">
<div class="accordion__item wysiwyg-text-align-justify">
<div class="accordion__item-title"><strong>Trust and Safety Initiatives and Partnerships - 2024 Second-Half Update</strong></div>
<div class="accordion__item-content">
<p>Our goal to achieve and set the highest level of Trust and Safety standards relies heavily on not only our internal policies and moderation team, but also on our array of external partnerships and technology. The organizations we partner with are part of the global effort to reduce illegal material online and help ensure our platform and adult users can feel safe.</p>
<p class="MsoNoSpacing"><span style="font-size: 11.0pt;">We continued to further our Trust and Safety efforts and are proud to have added new partnerships and initiatives. Below is a non-exhaustive list of these, for the period from July 1, 2024 through December 31, 2024: </span></p>
<p><strong>Co-Performer Verification Requirements</strong></p>
<p class="MsoNoSpacing"><span style="font-size: 11.0pt;">All members of our Model Program have already been required to maintain identity documentation and consent to record and distribute for every performer appearing in their content. Beginning in September 2024, all members of the model program became additionally required to provide our platform with evidence of those records for all new content, prior to its publication.</span></p>
<p><strong>Image-based Sexual Abuse Principles</strong></p>
<p>After the White House issued a <a href="https://www.whitehouse.gov/gpc/briefing-room/2024/05/23/a-call-to-action-to-combat-image-based-sexual-abuse/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Call to Action</a> to Combat Image-Based Sexual Abuse for tech and civil society on May 23, 2024, the Center for Democracy and Technology (CDT), the Cyber Civil Rights Initiative (CCRI), and the National Network to End Domestic Violence (NNEDV) invited civil society organizations and tech industry leaders to a multistakeholder working group (“<a href="https://cdt.org/press/cdt-ccri-and-nnedv-announce-multistakeholder-working-group-to-address-non-consensual-intimate-images/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Working Group</a>”) focused on combating IBSA.</p>
<p>Aylo participated in this working group, which worked to create a set of <a href="https://ibsaprinciples.org/">principles</a>, which were published in September 2024. We are proud of our continued work to prevent non-consensual content and hope that more organisations will sign-up to these voluntary principles.</p>
<p><strong>Identity Verification Providers</strong></p>
<p>In the second half of 2024 Aylo has conducted testing with an additional IDV provider, Incode. The use of Incode's service is expected to be deployed during the first half of 2025.</p>
<p> </p>
<p><span style="color: #111111;">For a full list of Trust and Safety partnerships, initiatives and external technology, please refer to our </span><a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/19159382668435-Trust-and-Safety-Initiatives">Trust and Safety Initiatives</a><span style="color: #111111;"> page.</span></p>
<p> </p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="accordion__item wysiwyg-text-align-justify">
<div class="accordion__item-title"><strong>Content Removals</strong></div>
<div class="accordion__item-content">
<p>A total of <strong>1.27 million</strong> (789,855 videos and 484,092 photos) pieces of content were uploaded to Pornhub in 2024 from July to December. <p>In the second half of 2024, we removed <strong>3,756 </strong>pieces of content (2,614 videos and  1,142 photos) for violating our <a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/4419871787027-Non-Consensual-Content-Policy">NCC policy</a>. <p>Our NCC policy includes the following violations:</p>
<ul>
<li>Non-Consensual Content – Act(s): Content which depicts activity for which an individual did not validly consent. A non-consensual act is one involving the application of force directly or indirectly without the consent of the other person to a sexual act. </li>

We report all instances of potential CSAM to the <a href="https://www.missingkids.org/">National Center for Missing and Exploited Children</a> (NCMEC).</p>
<p>In the last six months of 2024, we made <strong>4,037 </strong>reports to NCMEC. <div class="accordion__item-title"><strong>Moderation and Content Removal Process</strong></div>
<div class="accordion__item-content wysiwyg-text-align-justify">
<span class="wysiwyg-underline"><span class="wysiwyg-color-black wysiwyg-font-size-medium">Upload and Moderation Process</span></span>
<p>As Pornhub strives to prevent abusive material on our platform, only verified uploaders, including content partners and members of the Model Program can upload content to our site. All members of the Model Program are required to verify their identity via a third-party identity documentation validation and identity verification service provider. Once verified, <strong>all </strong>content is reviewed upon upload by our trained staff of moderators before it is ever made live on our site. Uploads are also automatically scanned against several automated detection technologies as well as our internal tool for fingerprinting and identifying violative content, Safeguard.</p>

<p>While users can notify us of potentially abusive content, we also invest a great deal into internal detection, which includes technology and a 24/7 team of moderators, who can detect content that may violate our Terms of Service at time of upload and before it is published. Most of this non-compliant content is discovered via our internal detection methods.</p>

<p>As we add technologies and new moderation practices, our goal is to ensure that our moderation team is identifying as much violative content as possible before it is published. <p><span style="color: #111111;">We are steadfast in our commitment to protecting the safety of our users and the integrity of our platform; we stand with all victims of non-consensual content. </span></p>
<p>From July through December, we removed 3,756 pieces of content (2,614 videos and  1,142 photos) for violating our <a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/4419871787027-Non-Consensual-Content-Policy">NCC policy</a>. </p>
<p class="MsoNormal">For all content removed for violating our NCC policy in the last six months of 2024, content was identified through both internal detection and user-sourced removals equally at 49.01%.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813300443923" alt="Source of removal_All NCC_24.png" width="592" height="363"></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure shows a breakdown of NCC removals based on the source of detection. In addition to internal and user-sourced removals, removals due to External Trusted Sources include legal requests and notifications from our </em><a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/4419879221907-Pornhub-Trusted-Flagger-Program"><em>Trusted Flaggers</em></a><em>. </em></span></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><strong><em>Analysis:</em></strong><em> Of all the content that was removed for violating our NCC policy in the last six months of 2024, including content uploaded prior to July 2024, nearly 49.01% of content was identified via Pornhub’s internal methods of moderation as well as an equal percentage(49.01%) of content being alerted to our team from our users.</em></span></p>
<p class="MsoNoSpacing">Most of the content uploaded in the last half of 2024 and removed for a violation of our NCC policy was identified through internal detection, at 88.04%.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813395275027" alt="Source of removal_NCC2024_24.png" width="591" height="362"></p>
<p class="MsoNormal"><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure shows a breakdown of NCC removals that were uploaded during the six-month period ending December 31, 2024, based on the source of detection. See above for further information about the sources of removal.</em></span></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><strong><em>Analysis:</em></strong><em> Of all the content that was uploaded and removed for violating our NCC policy during the last six months of 2024, 11.96% of content being alerted to our team from our users, compared to 88.04% of content identified via Pornhub’s internal methods of moderation. None of this content was removed due to notifications from External Trusted Sources.   </em></span></p>
<p><span style="color: black;">As part of our efforts to identify and quickly remove non-consensual content and other harmful material, we try to ensure this content is removed before it is available to users and consumers. Of videos both uploaded and removed for violating our NCC policy in 2024 from July through December, which represents 0.04% of videos uploaded during this time, over 81% were removed before being viewed.  </span></p>
<p>Videos uploaded in the last six months of 2024 and removed for violating our NCC policy accounted for 0.003% of total views of all videos uploaded in the second half of 2024.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813439355155" alt="NCC views_2024 uploads_24.png" width="590" height="355"></p>
<p class="MsoNormal"><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure shows the number of times videos uploaded in the last six months of 2024 were viewed prior to being removed for violating our NCC policy.</em></span></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><strong><em>Analysis:</em></strong><em> <span style="color: black; background-color: white;">Over 81% of videos were identified and removed by our human moderators or internal detection tools before going live on our platform.</span></em></span></p>
<p class="MsoNoSpacing"><span style="color: black;">We have continued to strengthen our policies surrounding uploader requirements for providing identity verification and consent documentation for all performers in content. As of September 2024, all members of the Model Program must submit this identity and consent documentation for every performer before their content can be published on Pornhub.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="accordion__item wysiwyg-text-align-justify">
<div class="accordion__item-title"><strong>Banned Accounts</strong></div>
<div class="accordion__item-content">
<p>As part of our efforts to ensure user and platform safety, we ban accounts that have committed serious or repeated violations of our <a href="https://www.pornhub.com/information/terms">Terms of Service</a>. Additionally, accounts that have violated our <a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/4419869793683-Child-Sexual-Abuse-Material-Policy">CSAM Policy</a> are reported to the <a href="https://www.missingkids.org/">National Center for Missing and Exploited Children</a> (NCMEC).</p>
<p>In the last six months of 2024, we banned a total of <strong>26,888 </strong>user accounts for violating our Terms of Service. This includes accounts that were banned for uploading content that was removed, as well as accounts that were banned for violations not related to content, such as spamming. Additionally, an account may be banned at the time of verification if we detect that the account belongs to an individual whose previous account was banned for violating our Terms of Service.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813542621331" alt="Accounts banned by reason.png" width="591" height="375"></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure shows the breakdown by ban reason for accounts that were banned in 2024 from July through December.</em></span></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em><strong>Analysis</strong>:</em><em> <span style="color: black; background-color: white;">Nearly 76% of accounts were banned for a Community Guidelines violation, while 7% of accounts were banned, as they were identified as belonging to an individual whose previous account(s) was/were banned.</span><span style="color: black; background-color: white;">  </span></em></span></p>
<p>The majority of accounts banned during this period were identified by our internal detection methods.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813587599251" alt="Source of removal_banned accounts.png" width="594" height="285"></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure shows a breakdown of banned accounts based on the source of detection. In addition to internal and user-sourced removals, removals due to External Trusted Sources include legal requests and notifications from our </em><a href="https://help.pornhub.com/hc/en-us/articles/4419879221907-Pornhub-Trusted-Flagger-Program"><em>Trusted Flaggers</em></a><em>.</em></span></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><strong><em>Analysis:</em></strong><em> Of the accounts that were banned in the last six months of 2024, nearly 92% were identified due to internal detection methods, while user notifications accounted for 6.12% of banned accounts.    </em></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="accordion__item wysiwyg-text-align-justify">
<div class="accordion__item-title"><strong>DMCA</strong></div>
<div class="accordion__item-content">
<p><span style="color: #111111; background-color: white;">The <em>Digital Millennium Copyright Act</em>, known as the DMCA, is an amendment to existing U.S. copyright law to address parts of its application on the internet. This includes establishing protections for online service providers if their users engage in copyright infringement, by creating a notice-and-takedown system which allows copyright owners to notify online services about infringement so that the material can be taken down. Service providers must have a process in place to receive DMCA notices and to remove applicable content and must have (and implement) a policy to deter infringement by enforcing a repeat infringement policy. Pornhub promptly responds to requests relating to copyright notifications. </span></p>
<p>In addition to blocking uploads of works previously fingerprinted with Mediawise or Safeguard from appearing on Pornhub, during the six-month period ending December 31,2024, we responded to <strong>422 </strong>requests for removal, leading to a total of <strong>539</strong> pieces of content (435 videos and 104 photos) removed.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813642489107" alt="DMCA received_24.png" width="599" height="354"></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure shows the number of requests for removal related to DMCA per month in the last half of 2024.</em></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="accordion__item wysiwyg-text-align-justify">
<div class="accordion__item-title"><strong>Cooperation with Law Enforcement</strong></div>
<div class="accordion__item-content">
<p>We cooperate with law enforcement globally and readily provide all information available to us upon request and receipt of appropriate documentation and authorization. Legal requests can be submitted by governments and law enforcement, as well as private parties.</p>
<p>In the second half of 2024, we responded to <strong>124 legal requests</strong>. A breakdown by request type as indicated by law enforcement is provided below.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813699574163" alt="Legal requests received_24.png" width="592" height="346"></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure displays the number of requests Pornhub received from law enforcement and legal entities in the last six months of 2024, broken down by the type of request as indicated by the requester.</em></span></p>
<p>As a result of these requests, we classified a total of <strong>51 pieces of content</strong> (30 videos and 21 photos) as Terms of Service Violations due to legal requests. A breakdown by removal type is provided below.</p>
<p><img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813693344787" alt="LR content removals_24.png" width="590" height="397"></p>
<p><span class="wysiwyg-font-size-small"><em>The above figure displays content that was identified in law enforcement requests that we deemed to violate our Terms of Service upon review.  </em></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="accordion__item wysiwyg-text-align-justify">
<div class="accordion__item-title"><strong>Content De-Indexing</strong></div>
<div class="accordion__item-content">
<p>As part of our Trust and Safety efforts to remove abusive content not only from our platform, but globally, we request de-indexing of URLs that were removed for violating our <a href="https://www.pornhub.com/information/terms">Terms of Service</a> from search engines. We proactively seek to de-index all content that is removed for potential CSAM and non-consensual content.</p>
<p>In the second half of 2024, we requested de-indexing of <strong>35,759 </strong>URLs for 17,768 unique pieces of content.<img src="/hc/article_attachments/38813750336147" alt="URLS_deindexed.png" width="595" height="361"></p>
<p class="MsoNoSpacing"><em><span style="font-size: 9.0pt;">The above figure displays a breakdown of the reason for URLs that were de-indexed from search engines. There may be several URLs de-indexed per piece of content, as we request the de-indexing of every version of the URL (e.g. it.pornhub.com/123 would be a URL de-indexed for the content located at www.pornhub.com/123). </span></em></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

              2024 Transparency Report (First Half)
            </h1>
            

            <div class="article-meta">
